title: Hero clarity grid — cross-segment messaging and test plan
body:
Purpose
---
A compact working brief to generate a set of homepage hero variants that prioritize clarity over cleverness. Goal: one set of concise claims + one-liners per audience segment, plus 6 concrete A/B test permutations (copy + CTA). This doc is intentionally terse — use as the single source for writing, creative, and experiments.

Context and thesis
---
- Problem we solve (short): Serving LLMs reliably at predictable latency and unit cost is a non-trivial engineering problem. Many teams either overpay for headroom or build brittle bespoke stacks.
- Core platform promise (single line): Predictable inference performance and cost—same API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Messaging constraint: Avoid abstract adjectives ("best", "fastest"). Focus on quantifiable levers: latency SLOs, cost controls, deployment options, and developer ergonomics.

Audience-specific positioning snapshots (one-liners + subheads)
---
1) Developer-first startups (PLG)
- Claim: "Ship LLM features without building a serving stack."
- Subhead: "One API for generation, embeddings, and reranking — scale from experimentation to production with predictable cost."
- Why it lands: speaks to speed-to-market, reduces infra work, and implies cost predictability.

2) Platform / infra teams
- Claim: "Standardize LLM inference across teams and clouds."
- Subhead: "Dedicated pools, private control planes, and routing policies that make inference an internal platform service."
- Why it lands: highlights governance, isolation, and operational consistency.

3) Enterprise product teams (regulated)
- Claim: "Secure, auditable inference that meets your compliance needs."
- Subhead: "Private deployments, KMS integrations, and audit-ready logs with SLA options for critical workloads."
- Why it lands: ties to procurement checkboxes: security, auditability, SLAs.

Hero clarity grid (copy primitives)
---
Use these as modular pieces to assemble variants. Keep each under ~70 characters for headline simplicity.
- Performance: "Predictable latency at scale"
- Cost: "Save on per-token spend with smart batching"
- Control: "Private deployments, enterprise controls"
- Simplicity: "One API for every inference need"
- Reliability: "Fallbacks and rollouts that keep apps online"
- Trust: "Audit logs, KMS, and region controls"

6 Variant recipes (headline + subhead + CTA)
---
Variant A (Developer velocity)
- Headline: "One API to ship LLM features faster"
- Subhead: "Generations, embeddings, and tools — with predictable latency and unit economics."
- CTA: "Try the API (free credits)"

Variant B (Cost-conscious proof)
- Headline: "Cut per-request cost with batching and cache"
- Subhead: "Automated batching, KV prefix caching, and quantization suggestions lower unit spend without degrading quality."
- CTA: "See estimated savings"

Variant C (Enterprise controls)
- Headline: "Private inference with enterprise SLAs"
- Subhead: "VPC-compatible private control plane, KMS, and audit logs — deploy on your terms."
- CTA: "Request a demo"

Variant D (Reliability-first)
- Headline: "Keep apps online with graceful fallbacks"
- Subhead: "Multi-variant routing and automatic fallbacks preserve service during capacity events."
- CTA: "Learn how fallbacks work"

Variant E (Unified operations)
- Headline: "One console for cost, latency, and rollouts"
- Subhead: "Per-route metrics, token-level cost breakdowns, and canary rollouts that make ops predictable."
- CTA: "Explore the console"

Variant F (Technical proofpoint)
- Headline: "GPU-optimized serving for modern transformer models"
- Subhead: "Optimized kernels, KV cache management, and quantization paths tuned for production workloads."
- CTA: "View performance specs"

Microcopy variations (small supporting lines)
---
- "Same API across hosted, dedicated, and private"
- "SLA-backed throughput and latency targets"
- "Per-token billing and cost breakdowns"
- "Canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies"

Competitive notes (short, internal-facing)
---
- Comp A: pricing-first APIs — good for quick dev tests but poor for enterprise controls. Position vs them: emphasize SLA and private deployment options.
- Comp B: self-hosted runtimes — strong on control, weak on dev ergonomics and observability. Position: highlight combined developer/ops experience and managed options.
- Comp C: cloud providers with managed endpoints — similar scale but often higher unit cost and less model-focused optimizations. Position: focus on per-token economics and model/kernel tuning.

Quantified trust hooks to test (choose 1 per headline)
---
- "<20ms median generation for chat workloads on p4-like hardware" (only use if we have verified benchmark)
- "Estimate: 30–50% lower token cost vs naive per-request serving" (back with internal calc)
- "99.95% uptime for Dedicated customers" (only if SLA available)

A/B test matrix (priority experiments)
---
- Test 1: Variant A vs Variant E for PLG landing page traffic — KPI: API signups, start-of-free-credit usage
- Test 2: Variant B vs Variant F on pricing page — KPI: pricing page CTA clicks, demo requests
- Test 3: Variant C (enterprise) vs Variant D on paid top-of-funnel — KPI: demo requests and form quality
- Segment routing: send enterprise-segment traffic to pages with C as default

Creative & visual notes
---
- Keep hero visual minimal: single abstract of "routing + cache" flow for developer hero; infrastructure audience sees a rack/map with regions and shields (security)
- Color/visual hierarchy: CTA style should map to user intent — primary CTA (free credits) green, secondary CTA (demo) blue

Open questions / decisions needed
---
- Do we want to include specific latency numbers in public-facing copy? (Legal/benchmarks needed)
- Which quantified cost-savings claim can be safely published? Need validation from Applied ML team.
- Should CTA language be uniform or segment-specific? Recommend segment-specific for higher relevance.

Immediate next steps (owners)
---
- Creative: produce 6 hero art variants (Marco) — due 2025-03-05
- Analytics: set experiment events and funnels (Sofia) — due 2025-03-03
- Applied ML: confirm or retract any public numeric claims (Evan) — due 2025-02-28

Notes to writer (tone + constraints)
---
- Tone: engineer-respectful, confident, not hyperbolic. Avoid marketing buzzwords without backing.
- Length: headline <= 8 words, subhead <= 18 words, microcopy <= 8 words.
- Accessibility: avoid color-only CTAs; alt text for hero visuals must be provided.

Scratch ideas (throwaway — keep minimal)
---
- "Serve, don't reinvent" — too cute? Might be ambiguous.
- "Make inference a platform primitive" — technical, could land with infra teams.
- Consider a permalinks row under hero with three micro-links: "Get started", "SLA & compliance", "Benchmarks"

End of brief
